## Overview

This model estimates a smooth association between sessions attended and word reading. Unlike the straight-line or period-specific slopes in [DOSE-077](../lrp-rli-dose-077/), a Hilbert-space Gaussian process (HSGP) allows the slope to vary across session counts. The exposure is measured in sessions attended within a period. The declared sampling target is `target_accept=0.999`.

**Exposure.** The model uses per-period attendance (`attend`). It excludes rows without an observed session count through the factory's exposure mask. Read the current row audit for the included children and periods.

## Adjustment set

Revised DAG (2026-07-10), re-derived by a backdoor d-separation search with the latent general ability ($GA$) held (the criterion that reproduces LRP58 and dose-077 exactly): $IS$'s parents are $\{A, GA, IG\}$ and nothing else, so the selected measured adjustment set is $\{A, IG\}$. Group $G\,(= IG)$ is the always-in term, $A$ the linear age precision covariate, and $W_{\text{pre}}$ the autoregressive baseline. The specification includes no measure, hearing or speech adjusters. This set does not remove the latent-ability confounding described below. This is **identical adjustment to dose-077** — only the functional form (HSGP curve vs period-varying slope) changes.

_Strictly observational — never a treatment effect._ Session dose was **not** randomised (how much a child attended reflects ability, attendance and availability) and $IS$ is a partial collider, so the curve is an **adjusted association / sensitivity view**, never a treatment effect. Residual confounding by latent general ability ($GA$) remains. Read the estimand as "how word reading differs across observed session counts, and whether that relationship bends" — **not** "more sessions cause faster progress". The corresponding randomised-arm result is an available-case modified ITT estimate in the ITT suite.
